newsitem.title: USA: No cold threat in Brazil coffee belt--Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: No cold threat in Brazil coffee belt--Smith Barney.

text.p: There is no threat of any frost or freeze damage to Brazil's coffee-growing areas during the next 10 days, Smith Barney meterologist Jon Davis said in his daily weather update on Tuesday.
A cold airmass will remain trapped across southern Argentina and Chile and will not penetrate northward up into areas of Brazil, he said.

"A weak pocket of cool air will ooze uo into Brazil this weekend as a small piece of cool air breaks off from the core of the polar air over the southern portion of South America," Davis said in his commentary. "This airmass poses no threat to the coffee crop since it is so weak."
Davis said temperatures will drop into the mid-40s to mid-50s F over the weekend, with no sign of any major cold airmasses moving into the region next week.
"The bottom line is that there is no frost/freeze damage threat during the next 10 days in Brazil," he said.
